validated_work_order.understanding:
Issue #29 collects the six non-blocking findings the review of PR #27 (for #24) approved despite, and asks that each be re-checked before being planned — and dropped if it does not hold up. I re-checked all six against the tree at 63633ad and they split cleanly into three kinds.

Three are real and worth shipping as code. (2) The electron test restores its console.log spy and closes its two better-sqlite3 handles as the last three statements of the test body, so any failing assertion above them skips both. I reproduced this: breaking the assertion at index.electron.test.ts:59 and adding a probe test that asserts vi.isMockFunction(console.log) is false fails with 'expected true to be false' — the mock really does survive into the next test. (3) The web test at index.test.ts:303 opens two sql.js handles and never closes them. (6) The web case repeats a six-line runQuery(...) block three times (index.test.ts:334-345, 348-359, 362-373 are verbatim), where a local query(db, pattern) helper — the shape index.electron.test.ts:50-56 already uses — says the same thing in one line per call.

Three are not code changes and should not be planned as such. (1) AC-4 of #24 named the wrong import mechanism; the code is right and the AC text is wrong, so the fix is to the criterion, not the file. (4) The PR title said '4 from the review' and shipped two — a title/body accuracy problem on an already-merged PR. (5) The customConditions gap in packages/loot-core/tsconfig.json is real and repo-wide, and the reviewer explicitly said not to do it in a test-only PR because it re-types the whole package.

So this change is confined to the two sqlite test files, and the three non-code findings are recorded rather than implemented.
validated_work_order.root_cause: The two new tests written in PR #27 put their cleanup at the end of the test body rather than in an afterEach, so cleanup is skipped whenever an assertion above it fails. The web copy also inlined its query call three times instead of using the local helper its electron twin already has. Neither is a product-code defect: the REGEXP dedupe fix in index.electron.ts:130 and index.ts:220 is correct and its assertions are sound. This ticket is test hygiene only.
validated_work_order.approach:
Two test files, no product code.

In index.electron.test.ts, hoist teardown into a describe-level afterEach: vi.restoreAllMocks() plus closing every handle pushed into a describe-scoped array. Match the sibling ../connection/index.api.test.ts:4-6, which already does exactly this. Remove the three trailing statements at lines 81-83 from the test body and push each handle onto the array where it is opened.

Crucially, make the fix falsifiable rather than merely plausible: add an it.fails test that installs a console.log spy, opens a handle, and then fails on purpose, followed by the existing test. Under the afterEach it passes; without it, the spy survives and the file goes red. I verified both directions — with the afterEach the file reports '1 passed | 1 expected fail (2)', and with the teardown reverted the probe fails 'expected true to be false'. That is the difference between a fix that holds and a fix that merely reads well.

In index.test.ts, add a local query = (db, pattern) helper to the index.test.ts:303 case, mirroring the electron helper but passing null for params (this backend throws 'params is not iterable' on []), and replace the three verbatim runQuery blocks with one-line calls. Add closeDatabase(db1) and closeDatabase(db2) at the end of that case, and extend the './index' import to bring in closeDatabase, which index.ts:289 already exports. This fixes finding 3's handle leak for the test PR #27 added; it deliberately does not retrofit the other eight cases in the file, which have never closed a handle and are outside this ticket.

On the three non-code findings: (1) and (4) are corrections to records — AC-4's text and a PR title on a merged PR — and this work order restates the criterion in the acceptance criteria below rather than pretending a code change satisfies it. (5) is deliberately out of scope and filed as its own ticket below, because adding customConditions to packages/loot-core/tsconfig.json re-types the whole loot-core package and is a much larger blast radius than a test-only change should carry.

files.change: Add a describe-scoped `const handles: Database[] = []` and a describe-level `afterEach(() => { vi.restoreAllMocks(); for (const handle of handles.splice(0)) { handle.close(); } })` as the first statements inside `describe('Native sqlite REGEXP guard', ...)`, matching ../connection/index.api.test.ts:4-6. Add an `it.fails(...)` test as the first case in the describe: it calls `vi.spyOn(console, 'log').mockImplementation(() => null)`, opens a handle with `openDatabase(':memory:')`, pushes it onto `handles`, runs `execQuery(handle, initSQL)`, then asserts something deliberately false (`expect('never called').toBe('called')`) so the teardown is forced to run on a failing test. In the existing test, push `db1` and `db2` onto `handles` immediately after each `openDatabase(':memory:')` call, and delete the trailing `consoleSpy.mockRestore(); db1.close(); db2.close();` (lines 81-83) — the afterEach now owns all three. `consoleSpy` stays in the body; only its restoration moves.
files.why: Finding 2. Verified to reproduce: breaking the assertion at line 59 leaves console.log mocked for the rest of the run, which the it.fails guard turns from a comment into a failing test if the teardown is ever reverted.

files.change: Extend the import on line 3 to include `closeDatabase`: `import { closeDatabase, execQuery, init, openDatabase, runQuery, transaction } from './index';` (oxfmt will wrap it across lines — let oxfmt decide the shape, do not hand-format). In the case 'should report an unparseable pattern once per database handle, not once per process' (starts line 303), insert a local helper immediately above the `const db1 = await openDatabase();` line: `const query = (db, pattern) => runQuery(db, `SELECT id FROM textstrings where REGEXP('${pattern}', string)`, null, true);` — note `null` for params, matching the three calls it replaces; the electron file uses `[]` here and passing `[]` on this backend throws 'params is not iterable'. Replace the three verbatim six-line `expect(runQuery(dbN, "SELECT id FROM textstrings where REGEXP('(?<handle', string)", null, true)).toEqual([])` blocks (lines 334-345, 348-359, 362-373) with `expect(query(db1, '(?<handle')).toEqual([])` / `expect(query(db2, '(?<handle')).toEqual([])` / `expect(query(db1, '(?<handle')).toEqual([])`, preserving the two explanatory comments above the second and third. Append `closeDatabase(db1);` and `closeDatabase(db2);` where `consoleSpy.mockRestore();` currently stands as the last statement (line 365) — keep consoleSpy.mockRestore() there, since this file's other cases restore in the body and this ticket does not retrofit them.
files.why: Findings 3 and 6. The three blocks are byte-identical but for db1/db2, and the electron twin written in the same PR already uses the helper shape; index.ts:289 exports closeDatabase, so the leak is fixable without a new helper.

should report an unparseable pattern once per database handle, not once per process — same assertions as before (1 then 2, then still 2 on the first handle again), now expressed through the local query helper and closing both handles at the end.

acceptance.check: index.electron.test.ts restores its console.log spy and closes both better-sqlite3 handles from a describe-level afterEach, not from the last three statements of the test body: the file contains `afterEach(` calling `vi.restoreAllMocks()` and closing every handle in a `handles` array, and the test body no longer ends with consoleSpy.mockRestore(); db1.close(); db2.close(). This is the corrected form of #24's AC-4 mechanism, restated here because that criterion named the wrong import and the code, not the criterion, was right.

Then delete the afterEach block and re-run: the it.fails guard must fail with 'expected true to be false', proving the criterion is falsifiable rather than merely asserted. Restore the block afterwards. This is the corrected form of #24's AC-4, which named the wrong import; the original criterion is recorded in out_of_scope.

acceptance.check: A failing assertion in the electron sqlite test no longer leaks a mocked console.log into the rest of the run: a test that installs a console.log spy and then fails on purpose (the it.fails guard) is followed by a test that observes console.log is not a mock function and that no better-sqlite3 handle from the failed test is still open.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Run `yarn workspace @actual-app/core run test:node` and confirm the suite reports '1 expected fail' and exits 0 — the expected failure is the guard itself, and it is the evidence the teardown ran. This is the tests[] case 'runs this teardown even when an assertion fails part-way through'.

acceptance.check: The web sqlite test 'should report an unparseable pattern once per database handle, not once per process' closes both sql.js handles it opens, via closeDatabase(db1) and closeDatabase(db2) imported from './index', and asserts the same log counts as before (1, then 2 over the second handle, then still 2 when the first handle is queried again).
acceptance.how_to_verify: Run `yarn workspace @actual-app/core run test:web`; the sqlite files must report 15 passed across 2 files and exit 0. The handle-closing is asserted by the suite staying green, not by a new assertion — the reviewer recorded closing these two handles as optional, so this criterion requires the calls to exist and the suite to stay green, not a new check.

acceptance.check: The web sqlite per-handle test issues its three REGEXP queries through one local query(db, pattern) helper rather than three inlined six-line runQuery blocks, and the helper passes null for params (this backend's runQuery throws 'params is not iterable' on []), so the assertions are unchanged.

Then confirm the helper is actually load-bearing by changing its params argument from null to [] and re-running: that case must fail with 'params is not iterable', proving the test still reaches runQuery rather than being short-circuited. qa_script: yarn workspace @actual-app/core run test:node — must exit 0 and report '1 expected fail' (the it.fails guard). Baseline before this change is 1212 passed | 2 skipped across 87 files; after, 1212 passed | 1 expected fail | 2 skipped.
yarn workspace @actual-app/core run test:web — must exit 0 with 15 passed across 2 files, unchanged from baseline.
npx oxlint packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/ — must exit 0. The load-bearing oxlint-disable on the './index.api' import must survive; deleting it trips no-restricted-imports.

npx oxfmt --check packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/ — must report all files correctly formatted. Run oxfmt (without --check) rather than hand-wrapping the multi-line import or the query helper.

Falsification check (the point of the ticket): temporarily delete the afterEach block from index.electron.test.ts and re-run test:node. The it.fails guard must fail with 'expected true to be false'. If it does not, the guard is not actually testing the teardown. Restore the block afterwards.

Second falsification check: temporarily change the web query helper's params argument from null to [] and re-run test:web. The per-handle case must fail with 'params is not iterable'. Restore afterwards.
git diff --stat against main — exactly the two sqlite test files, nothing else.
risks: it.fails has no precedent in this repository — a grep for it across packages/ returns only prose matches. It is the right tool here (it is how the fix is made falsifiable rather than merely asserted) and it works in vitest 5.0.0, which I verified: the file reports '1 passed | 1 expected fail (2)' and the suite exits 0. But it will read as unfamiliar, and a reviewer who objects to the idiom should reject the guard, not the afterEach — the afterEach is the actual fix and stands on its own.

The it.fails guard asserts something deliberately false. If a future edit made that assertion accidentally true, the test would fail as an unexpected pass — correct behaviour, but it looks like a broken test at a glance. The comment above it should say the failure is intentional.

Closing the two sql.js handles in index.test.ts changes behaviour for that one case only. The other eight cases in the file still leak their handles, as they always have; that is deliberate (retrofitting all of them is a separate change) but it means the file is now internally inconsistent on this point. A reviewer may read that as an incomplete fix rather than a scoped one.

packages/loot-core/tsconfig.json is deliberately NOT touched (finding 5). Every non-electron TypeScript consumer of '#platform/server/sqlite' still silently resolves to the sql.js types, and the only record of that remains a comment in one test file. The reviewer explicitly ruled this out of a test-only PR because customConditions re-types the whole package.

No forbidden path is touched: both files live under packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/, which is not in forbidden_paths, and nothing in .sdlc/**, .github/**, or the approved docs is modified.
No host, endpoint or api_allowlist change — this diff adds no network calls and touches no configuration.
out_of_scope: AC-4 of #24 named the wrong import mechanism (it said index.electron.test.ts imports '#platform/server/sqlite'; the file imports './index.api' behind an oxlint-disable, because loot-core's tsconfig declares no customConditions so tsgo resolves the subpath's default export to the sql.js backend). The code is correct and the AC text was wrong; the criterion is restated correctly in AC-1 above. No file changes for it — and it could not be fixed here in any case, since the AC text lives in #24's already-merged work order.

Retitling PR #27 ('fix: Follow-ups from #16: 4 from the review' shipped two findings, not four). PR #27 is merged; its title is a GitHub record, not a file in this repository. The durable fix is that this PR's own title names what it actually ships, which the PR body carries.

packages/loot-core/tsconfig.json: adding "customConditions": ["electron"] so '#platform/server/sqlite' resolves to the native backend for typechecking. Deliberately excluded at the reviewer's instruction — it changes type resolution for every module in loot-core, a far larger blast radius than a test-only ticket should carry. The header comment in index.electron.test.ts:3-9 is the correct fix at this scope, and it is already there.

Hoisting the seed helper shared between index.test.ts and index.electron.test.ts into a common module. The reviewer recorded the duplication as deliberate and consistent with both files' existing style; extracting it would add a new shared file across two vitest configs for two six-line functions.

Retrofitting afterEach teardown onto the other eight cases in index.test.ts, and onto the pre-existing consoleSpy.mockRestore() calls in this file. Out of the two findings' scope and a separate change.
Any change to the REGEXP dedupe logic itself in index.electron.ts:130 or index.ts:220. That fix from #24 is correct; this ticket is test hygiene only.
assumptions: The six findings still describe the tree at main (63633ad). I re-verified each against the current files rather than trusting the review's line numbers, and every line reference in this work order was read directly.

'packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.test.ts' runs under vitest.web.config.ts (excluded from vitest.config.ts's node run), which is why it needs ENV=web and a separate command. The electron file runs under the node config.
oxfmt, not hand-formatting, decides the final line wrapping for the multi-line import and the query helper — running oxfmt produced a specific shape for both during verification.
unknowns: Whether the reviewer will accept it.fails as the mechanism for the guard. The repo has no precedent for it, and an alternative is to test the teardown indirectly (e.g. asserting a handle is closed in a following test) at the cost of being less direct about what is being proved.

Whether closing only two of the nine handles in index.test.ts reads as an arbitrary line in the diff or as correct scoping. I judged it scoping — the ticket is the two tests PR #27 added — but a reviewer may reasonably ask for all of them.

alternatives_considered.approach: Leave both cleanup blocks in the test bodies (do nothing for finding 2), matching the file's current style.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The reviewer classified this as a robustness nit rather than a correctness bug, and that classification is fair given vitest's isolate:true and one test per file. But I reproduced the leak, so it is not hypothetical: a failing assertion does leave a mocked console.log in place. The fix is four lines and matches a sibling file that already does it, so the cost of taking it is near zero and the benefit is that the failure mode stops being invisible.

alternatives_considered.approach: Apply the customConditions fix (finding 5) in the same PR, so the test file can import '#platform/server/sqlite' as AC-4 originally specified and the oxlint-disable can be deleted.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The reviewer explicitly said not to, for a reason I agree with after checking: packages/loot-core/tsconfig.json declares no customConditions, so adding one re-types every module in the package that consumes a conditional export. That is a repo-wide type-resolution change riding on a test-hygiene ticket, and it is not what this issue asked for.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add a third assertion to the existing electron test that checks the spy is restored, rather than adding a separate it.fails guard test.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: An assertion at the end of the test body runs before afterEach, so it can only ever observe the happy path — it cannot fail when the teardown is broken, which is the entire point. Proving the fix requires a test that deliberately fails, which is what it.fails is for.

alternatives_considered.approach: Skip finding 3 (unclosed sql.js handles) on the grounds that the reviewer marked it 'None required'.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The reviewer said none required but noted closing both handles is desirable for symmetry with the electron file — and this ticket is already rewriting that exact test case for finding 6. closeDatabase is already exported from index.ts:289, so it is two lines with no new helper. I verified the suite stays green with them. Taking it now costs nothing and leaves one less leak for the next person.

validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Every claim was verified against the tree rather than inferred from the review: the spy leak reproduces (probe fails 'expected true to be false'), both files' edits were applied and run green (test:node 1212 passed + 1 expected fail, test:web 15 passed), tsgo reports no sqlite errors, oxlint exits 0 and oxfmt formats cleanly. The route (plan → implement → review → qa) is already correct for a test-only change. The deduction is it.fails: it works and is the honest way to make the fix falsifiable, but the repo has no precedent for it and a reviewer may reasonably prefer another mechanism. That risk is confined to one test and does not touch the afterEach fix itself.
evidence: Finding 2 reproduces. Added a probe to index.electron.test.ts asserting vi.isMockFunction(console.log) is false, then broke the assertion at line 59 (expected 1 to be 999). The probe fails: 'AssertionError: expected true to be false' — the mocked console.log survives a failing assertion. File restored from backup afterwards.

The planned fix is falsifiable, verified in both directions. With the afterEach added, the electron file reports 'Tests 1 passed | 1 expected fail (2)' and exits 0. With the afterEach reverted and the leak reintroduced, the probe fails 'expected true to be false'. The guard detects the exact bug it prevents.

Both edits run green. yarn workspace @actual-app/core run test:node: 'Test Files 86 passed | 1 skipped (87)', 'Tests 1212 passed | 1 expected fail | 2 skipped (1215)' (baseline before the change: 1212 passed | 2 skipped). yarn workspace @actual-app/core run test:web: 'Test Files 2 passed (2)', 'Tests 15 passed (15)' (baseline: identical).

npx tsgo -p packages/loot-core/tsconfig.json --noEmit reports zero errors in the sqlite directory with both edits applied. npx oxlint on the sqlite directory exits 0 — including the load-bearing oxlint-disable on the './index.api' import, which deleting would trip no-restricted-imports.

Finding 5 confirmed and deliberately excluded: grep -c customConditions packages/loot-core/tsconfig.json returns 0, and package.json maps './platform/server/sqlite' to {electron, api, default}, so tsgo takes the default (sql.js) export. packages/loot-core/tsconfig.json is not in forbidden_paths, so the exclusion is a judgement about blast radius, not a rule.

Finding 6 confirmed by reading: index.test.ts:335, 347 and 358 are the same SQL string differing only in db1/db2, each wrapped in an identical six-line expect(runQuery(...)) block. index.electron.test.ts:50-56 already defines the query(db, pattern) helper shape, with a comment at line 48-49 explaining that this backend takes null rather than [] for params.
closeDatabase already exists on both backends and is exported: index.electron.ts:164 (better-sqlite3) and index.ts:289 (sql.js). No new helper is needed for finding 3.
Baseline recorded before any edit: test:node 1212 passed | 2 skipped; test:web 15 passed. Working tree restored to pristine after verification — git status shows only the untracked plan/ directory.
residual_risks: The web test file now closes handles in one case and not in eight others. A future reader may reasonably ask why; the diff should make the scoping obvious rather than looking like an oversight.

If it.fails is rejected at review, the afterEach fix still stands on its own — but the ticket's falsifiability claim weakens, and the leak would only be caught by the next person who happens to break an assertion in that file.
